debrief.text:
Analyst
-------
  [info] R7 was the match's pivotal round -- the largest single swing (0.201) in the win-probability proxy. Blue took it, Red lost it.
           rule: analyst.pivotal_round, 4 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Red reached a plant in only 42% of its attack rounds -- most of those rounds were lost before the spike ever went down.
           rule: analyst.plant_rate, 1 feature row(s) cited

Economist
---------
  [critical] Blue broke its buy 4 times (R6, R11, R15, R19) -- rounds where the escalated loss bonus should have funded a real buy and the team went in short anyway.
           rule: economist.broken_buy_count, 4 feature row(s) cited
  [critical] Red broke its buy 2 times (R2, R9) -- rounds where the escalated loss bonus should have funded a real buy and the team went in short anyway.
           rule: economist.broken_buy_count, 2 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue force-bought in 10 of 24 rounds (42%), past the 30% mark where forcing stops being a read and starts being a habit.
           rule: economist.force_buy_frequency, 24 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Red force-bought in 8 of 24 rounds (33%), past the 30% mark where forcing stops being a read and starts being a habit.
           rule: economist.force_buy_frequency, 24 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Red was out-spent by Blue by 1690 credits across the match's 24 rounds -- roughly a third of a full team buy in equipment Red never got to bring.
           rule: economist.spend_disadvantage, 24 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Blue stole 1 of its 1 eco rounds (100%).
           rule: economist.eco_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Red stole 0 of its 1 eco rounds (0%).
           rule: economist.eco_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited

provenance.detail: val-match-v1 requires a Riot production key. Matches here are generated by an in-repo simulator that emits payloads in the documented val-match-v1 shape, grounded in real agent and map UUIDs fetched live from val-content-v1. Nothing is scraped and no unofficial API is used. Every module downstream of the match adapter is source-agnostic, so live data swaps in with no code change.
provenance.note: Simulated data conforming to the val-match-v1 schema — production key application pending
